items.summary: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) have extended their capabilities beyond lexical speech understanding to tasks requiring paralinguistic and non-linguistic audio understanding, such as emotion recognition. However, these models still struggle to reliably utilize acoustic information, particularly when it co-occurs with spoken linguistic content. Existing benchmarks do not clearly distinguish acoustic perception from higher-level reasoning, making it difficult to identify the source of these failures. To address this issue, we introduce VocalGrad, a benchmark designed to evaluate LALMs' ability to perceive low-level acoustic variations. VocalGrad formulates this problem as a simple binary classification of temporal change direction, enabling evaluation largely independent of higher-level reasoning or semantic understanding. Our benchmark results reveal a substantial gap in acoustic perception between human annotators and state-of-the-art LALMs: while human annotators achieve high accuracy, LALMs perform at near-chance levels. We further conduct linear probing to identify structural bottlenecks in these models. Our analysis reveals two distinct failure modes: for some categories, task-relevant information is preserved in internal representations but not utilized by the language model head; for others, the information becomes progressively less linearly decodable across model layers. Overall, our results reveal substantial limitations of LALMs in modeling acoustic variation under controlled settings and expose representation differences not observable from text outputs.
items.title: VocalGrad: Evaluating Acoustic Perception in Audio Language Models

items.summary: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.
items.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness

items.summary: Emergency-stop circuits built by engineering technology students are routinely treated as safe once they pass a functional test at commissioning, yet the relay contact welding that dominates their failure modes is invisible to such tests and accumulates silently across the workshop's operating life. The framework represents a student-built circuit as a series safety function whose integrity is degraded by contact welding, and derives the conditions under which a welded contact converts a demanded stop into an undetected loss of safety function. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator was conducted under a declared variance structure with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The evaluation indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect at 80% power falls as the number of clusters rises. The framework proposes that workshop safety assurance should shift from commissioning-time functional testing to integrity monitoring that is sensitive to contact welding, and the design analysis implies that cluster-level evaluations of such interventions require cluster counts well above those typical of single-institution studies.
tags: emergency-stop circuits; functional safety; relay contact welding; fault injection; injury-risk expo
items.title: Functional-Safety-Integrity Degradation of Student-Built Emergency-Stop Circuits in Engineering Technology Education Workshops: A Fault-Injection Evaluation Linking Relay Contact Welding to Operator Injury-Risk Exposure

items.summary: Finite-element models, extracted results, analysis scripts and figure scripts supporting the article "Competing Failure Modes in Residually Stressed Thin Films on Flexible Substrates: Wrinkling, Channel Cracking, and Their Coupling" (International Journal of Solids and Structures). All finite-element calculations are carried out with ABAQUS/Standard 2021: the plane-strain linear-buckling benchmark and the geometrically nonlinear post-buckling sweep (imperfection, phase and mesh), the channel-crack factor and stress field, the J-integral and cohesive-zone crest-crack models, the three-dimensional stripe, checkerboard, hexagonal and herringbone wrinkle patterns, and the Al/Al2O3 equi-biaxial unit cell. The archive contains the input-generation scripts, input files, ODB post-processing scripts, results in JSON format, solver logs, the Python scripts that reproduce Figures 1–17 of the article, the figures, a README, a figure-to-source map, software versions and a SHA-256 file manifest. The three zip files unpack into one folder, thin_film_failure_modes_data.
items.title: Data and code for "Competing Failure Modes in Residually Stressed Thin Films on Flexible Substrates: Wrinkling, Channel Cracking, and Their Coupling"

items.summary: Sixteen commits since v1.0.0 (2026-07-05). The pipeline was run end to end for the first time on the current Claude Science product in this window — ComputationalReviewSSTdisease — and most of what follows comes from defects that run exposed. Runtime Runs with nothing to install: the coordinator saves skills/*.md as artifacts at session start and hands sub-agents the skill files they need (new "Runtime: Claude Science" section in the orchestrator). LITREVIEW and DATAML are roles delegated to default sub-agents, not profiles. Legacy delegate_to / operon.* / pipeline.* calls updated to host.* (#5). All 20 skills carry name / description frontmatter. Fixes found by running the pipeline Authorship widget published empty. The Phase 14 instruction said :authors: ../authors.yml ; the plugin resolves that path relative to the document directory, and 00_frontmatter.md and authors.yml both live in content/ . Corrected to ./authors.yml , with the silent-failure mode documented (#5). Evidence Database page published empty from a complete evidence set, with a green build. Four independent faults: the plugin never followed the v29 evidence_section_NN.json rename, looped sections 02..13 , read argument_groups.*.supporting_findings cite-key strings as finding records, and swallowed every read failure in catch { continue } . It now discovers the section files present, accepts all three historical naming conventions, prefers ev.findings , and throws rather than publishing empty (#6). Build failed on an un-instantiated evidence directory. A directory with no JSON at all is now treated as a template awaiting a run and renders a placeholder; JSON present but matching no package name stays fatal (#8). comprev-scoping.md 's description frontmatter was truncated mid-sentence (#5). Version management The pipeline generation number lived in a filename and in ~20 loose strings, while the only release tag described itself as "Expert Review Pipeline v29". The generation now lives solely in skills/manifest.json , which also records the sha256 and byte count of every skill file; the release version lives solely in git tags and is written into no file (#7). scripts/build_skill_manifest.py generates and verifies the manifest — standard library only — and a Skill manifest workflow runs --check on every push and pull request. It fails on a skill edited without a manifest regeneration, a version-bearing skill filename, a frontmatter name that disagrees with its filename, a description quoting the wrong generation, or a README naming a generation the manifest does not. Session setup writes provenance/pipeline_version.json into each review (generation, template commit, template tag, manifest hash, per-skill artifact ids). Phase 1's review_request.md header, Methods M.8 and pipeline_metrics.json read the version from that file instead of carrying a typed-in number. Renamed skills/comprev-orchestrator-v29.md → skills/comprev-orchestrator.md . Update saved prompts that name the old path. Nothing depends on this repository programmatically, and reviews already produced carry their own copy of skills/ , so they are unaffected.
items.title: AllenNeuralDynamics/ComputationalReviewTemplate: v1.1.0

items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode: a goal-directed builder and an exists-forall search, each followed by an independent gate. From the rules of Steinberg's problem it rebuilds the gadgets of the 2016 counterexample of Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado; it finds nothing on Erdős's question for cycles of length 4 to 6. Layer towers of depth one to three, a ladder and a mesh, are compared with the crossing loop at the same number of checks. A Hodge-only run of twelve rounds leaves every target point at the same gap. None of the five benchmark problems (the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture, Erdős problem 1183) is solved. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.
items.title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

items.summary: We study unitary \(S^1\)-manifolds with four isolated fixed points in relation to Kosniowski's conjectural inequality \(4χ(M)>\dim M\). For every integer \(m\ge3\), we show that there exists a unitary \(S^1\)-manifold \(M_m^{18}\) with exactly four isolated fixed points, and these manifolds are pairwise distinct and nonzero in ordinary complex bordism. Since \(χ(M_m^{18})=4\), they give an infinite family of counterexamples to \(4χ(M)>\dim M\). By gluing two blocks formed by \(G_2/SU(3)\cong S^6\) and the unit disk $D(V)$ of 12- dimensional real $S^1$-representation $V$ along their equivariantly identified free boundaries, we explicitly construct such a manifold $M^{18}_3$. We also prove that the four-point case is null-bordant in real dimension \(16\) and in every real dimension greater than \(18\); hence \(18\) is the smallest dimension in which such a counterexample occurs.
items.title: Unitary $S^1$-Manifolds with Four Fixed Points and Kosniowski's Conjecture

items.summary: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe. Despite this progress, success rates remain low, and it is unclear which capability these fine-tuned policies lack. Our diagnosis identifies goal grounding as the dominant failure. These policies explore well, yet often fail to notice that the goal is already in view or to estimate how far away it is. To address this failure, we ground the goal explicitly. Explicit grounding substantially improves success and reaches state-of-the-art results on six benchmarks across three scene collections. We also correct annotation defects in these benchmarks, so that future methods are evaluated more faithfully. Our analysis on the clean benchmarks shows that, with ground-truth grounding, our policy nearly matches the expert that generated its demonstrations, leaving the headroom in perception rather than policy learning. Our work points to goal grounding as a missing piece of object-goal navigation and offers a simple and effective solution to the task.
items.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation

items.summary: Diffusion-based multimodal large language models (dMLLMs) decode by iterative denoising with bidirectional attention, which precludes the standard autoregressive key--value cache. Practical deployments therefore rely on approximate caching that reuses intermediate states across denoising steps. Such caching, however, often makes a response repeat one token at adjacent positions in a run that breaks the sentence, a failure we term the \emph{Repeat Curse}. Tracing the context-token information flow reveals three disruptions. Within a step, caching disperses the attention that anchors a position on nearby context tokens. Across steps, similarity-based refresh is not staleness-aware, so some positions are decoded against stale key--value states. Across layers, the deep-layer entropy of the context fails to converge where repetition arises. We accordingly propose CoTA++, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that counteracts each disruption where it originates: Context-Token Attention Re-anchoring re-forms the attention routing against the current context, Decode-Aware Refresh reserves part of the cache's refresh budget for the positions about to be committed, and Context-Token Entropy-Guided Voting discounts the confidence of a position by the deep-layer entropy of its context, which reorders the unmasking. The three components act at non-overlapping stages of a decoding step and compose freely with existing dMLLMs and caches. Across three dMLLMs and two caching backends, CoTA++ reduces the sample repetition rate of long responses from up to 99.6\% to at most 17.0\%, recovers most of the accuracy lost to caching on nine benchmarks, and keeps the speedup of caching at under 15\% overhead, making approximate caching reliable for dMLLMs.
items.title: CoTA++: Understanding the Repeat Curse in dMLLMs from an Information Flow Perspective

items.summary: The High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE) onboard the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) acquires imagery of Mars at 25--30 cm/pixel, supporting studies of martian geology, climate history, and landing-site characterization. Its 14-detector focal plane assembly includes several overlapping detectors that enable the acquisition of three-channel colour-infrared images, which are important for identifying compositional variations and studying active surface processes. In 2023, a detector in the center of the focal plane assembly (RED4) began failing intermittently, creating a gap in acquired imagery and reducing the instrument's colour-imaging capability by half. The HiRISE processing pipeline provides a synthetic red (SYN4) channel obtained by linearly scaling the co-located infrared (IR10) channel. However, this approach cannot capture observed non-linear relationships between the colour channels, limiting its accuracy and applicability. Here, we present HiPredict, a machine-learning framework that reconstructs RED4 from co-located IR10 and blue-green (BG12) imagery, neighbouring red-channel observations, and acquisition metadata. The model employs a U-Net architecture to learn non-linear spatiotemporal-spectral relationships between these inputs and is trained on 81,717 training samples, representing 13,625 observations. Evaluated on 23,348 test samples, representing 3,892 pre-failure observations, HiPredict reconstructs RED4 with a Normalised Mean Absolute Error of 1.1%, substantially outperforming SYN4 (3.1%). The reconstructed products improve colour image recovery and more closely represent features of interest such as icy craters, stratigraphy exposed along ridge crests and chloride deposits. We release HiPredict as an open software tool. This work demonstrates the potential of machine learning to mitigate data loss as planetary missions age and naturally degrade.
items.title: HiPredict: Predicting the missing HiRISE RED4 spectral channel with machine learning

items.summary: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.
items.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses

items.title: bartulem/usv-playpen: v0.13.0

items.summary: Relational out-of-distribution errors are easy to describe and hard to evaluate cleanly. An image may be natural, a caption may be fluent, and all mentioned objects may be common, yet the caption may describe the wrong relation in the image. Many evaluations intended to test this behavior can be solved without checking the pairing at all, because negatives differ in caption style, template, length, object frequency, or image statistics. We propose counterfactual pairing cycles, a blocked evaluation primitive that reuses the same two images and the same two captions on both sides of the comparison, changing only which image is paired with which caption. This makes image-only, text-only, and additive component shortcuts cancel exactly in finite samples. The same contrast also gives a training loss for relational outlier exposure and a diagnostic for bilinear vision-language scores. Across synthetic controls, GQA, and COCO, cycles separate coarse image-caption matching from directional role-binding failures, while also identifying geometric size relations that remain strongly visible in global features. In a shortcut-contaminated COCO outlier-exposure stress test, a model selected by a near-perfect shortcut validation AUROC retains substantial relational signal but remains below cycle training on exact cycles; cycle training improves CycleAcc from 0.882 to 0.927. The main lesson is simple: to test whether a model understands a pairing, the benchmark should keep the parts fixed, change the pairing, and ask only about coupling. The official implementation is available online.
items.title: Can the Parts Fool the Test? Counterfactual Pairing Cycles for Relational OOD

items.summary: Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability. We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long-horizon reasoning. Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression-Think-Action (CTA) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason. The same model, given privileged multi-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student-generated CTA rollouts. Our Perception-Memory Fidelity (PMF) Gap-guided OPD-RL framework dynamically balances privileged distillation and task-reward optimization, with periodic teacher updates supporting continued improvement. We further introduce ECHOESBMK, a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark derived from real GUI agent failure trajectories to jointly evaluate visual perception and cross-modal state retention. Experiments on four GUI benchmarks and ECHOESBMK demonstrate substantial gains in task performance and memory fidelity. Without retaining historical screenshots at deployment, ECHOES achieves competitive performance with a favorable performance-inference-cost trade-off and exhibits positive zero-shot transfer to unseen visual planning tasks.
items.title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation

items.summary: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) and ischaemia with non-obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA) are increasingly recognised syndromes in which endothelial dysfunction forms the mechanistic bridge between vascular biology and clinical ischaemia. In health, the endothelium preserves vascular homeostasis by regulating tone, platelet activity, and inflammation; when this regulation fails, vessels assume a pro-constrictive, pro-thrombotic, and pro-inflammatory state capable of causing epicardial vasospasm, microvascular dysfunction, or plaque erosion—provoking genuine infarction and arrhythmias despite unobstructed arteries. This paper follows the continuum from these mechanisms to their clinical expression. It traces the evolution from early angiographic observations to contemporary imaging such as CMR, IVUS, and OCT, and outlines a chronological diagnostic pathway from the emergency department to the catheterisation laboratory. Subtle but actionable clues are highlighted across the clinical history, ECG, echocardiography, and angiography, demonstrating that a positive, mechanism-based diagnosis of endothelial dysfunction is feasible even when invasive testing is unavailable. Management is directed by the dominant mechanism calcium-channel blockers and nitrates for vasospastic angina; β-blockers or metabolic agents for microvascular angina supported by endothelial stabilisers, cardiac rehabilitation, and psychosocial care. Persistent endothelial dysfunction is associated with later heart-failure development, particularly HFpEF, emphasising the need     for   early   recognition     and     tailored   therapy.   The  chapter concludes with real-world challenges and emerging perspectives, including standardised testing, AI-assisted imaging, and precision therapeutics. Ultimately, understanding endothelial dysfunction links mechanisms to clinical practice, reframing MINOCA and INOCA as diagnosable and treatable syndromes that demand mechanism-based, preventive care.
tags: Endothelial dysfunction; MINOCA; INOCA; Coronary microvascular dysfunction; Vasospastic angina; Hear
items.title: Endothelial Dysfunction in Myocardial Infarction With Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries and Ischemia With Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries: Mechanisms and Clinical Approach

items.summary: EIP-1559 has become the dominant transaction fee mechanism in permissionless blockchains, regulating scarce block space through an adaptive base fee. The design balances a trade-off between responsiveness to demand fluctuations and stability of long-term resource usage. On a single chain, this trade-off is well understood and empirically stable. In multi-chain systems, however, cross-chain flows introduce delayed economic interactions across otherwise independent fee markets. These interactions alter the control dynamics and create stability risks that existing models do not capture. Deployed systems have already polarized. Polkadot enforces conservative update rates, effectively disabling fee adaptivity and reverting the market to inefficient first-price auctions. Cosmos adopts aggressive update rates without formal guarantees. To fill this gap, we propose a control-theoretic framework that formalizes multi-chain fee markets as a nonlinear dynamical system with delayed feedback. We identify delay-amplified over-correction as the structural root of instability. Experiments show that cross-chain coupling erodes stability relative to monolithic blockchains, reducing the safe parameter space for base fee update rates by up to 84.8%. Moreover, instability propagates across chains, contaminating the otherwise stable peer chains. At Ethereum's update rate, which leaves a monolithic chain stable, the multi-chain system exhibits extreme load oscillation between full and near-empty blocks, with over half of all blocks at full capacity. Mainstream Cosmos chains already exceed their safe bounds under their default configurations, and the resulting load oscillation raises their block failure rate by an order of magnitude. Guided by this mechanism, we design a lightweight protocol-level mitigation that removes the over-correction and stabilizes dynamics in multi-chain environments.
items.title: On the (In)stability of Adaptive Fee Mechanisms in Multi-Chain Systems

items.summary: Which biological findings enter a reported explanation depends on how the model population was constructed, a choice predictive validation alone does not reveal. We fitted 10,000 L2-regularised logistic regression models to TCGA pan-cancer tumour-versus-normal data: 100 regularisation strengths on 100 train-test splits, with patients fixed within each split. Strongly and weakly regularised models differ in mean accuracy by only 0.21 percentage points, yet prioritise different genes systematically with regularisation strength. Averaging explanations across a hyperparameter grid produces a top-50 panel sharing 41 genes with a single fitted model, but which model depends on the grid centre (Spearman correlation 0.92, 350 simulated practitioners). For 43 of 50 practitioners, the panel combines genes from strongly and weakly regularised models more fully than any fitted model: the explanation belongs to no model whose accuracy was established. A conventional grid recovers only a quarter of genes favoured exclusively by the strongest regularisation. HMGCS2 ranks among the top 50 in 73 of 100 strongly regularised fits and no weakly regularised fits, yet appears in none of 50 simulated reports. Reconstructing a published biomarker workflow on 20 cohort resamples reveals a different failure: the closest refit contains only 23 of the averaged panel's 50 genes, and no panel gene appears in all 20 refits. We define model-relative provenance as how much of a panel any single fitted model contains, distinct from workflow provenance recording how an analysis was run. We provide measurements to make the model population, the choice that selects from it, and that provenance reportable.
items.title: Same Accuracy, Different Gene Panels: How the Hyperparameter Grid Chooses the Reported Explanation

items.summary: INTEGRATED PHOTONIC MICROROBOTIC SYSTEMS AT THE LIMIT FLAGSHIP 16 / 30 | STARLI RESEARCH INSTITUTE XXIV This prospective research monograph investigates whether silicon-photonic light distribution, optofluidic packaging, independent metrology, and feedback positioning can be integrated into a compact research station that reliably captures, transports, releases, and recovers microscopic proxy agents. Its central hypothesis is system-level rather than decorative: reducing external optics is a meaningful advance only when delivered optical power, fluid transport, sample heating, task outcomes, and failure responses remain independently observable and reproducible across fabricated chip and package lots. The study develops a five-layer research architecture encompassing packaged optical and fluidic paths; a physically bounded optical-power and thermal ledger; external tracking capable of challenging on-chip estimates; reversible multi-agent tasks under staged fault injection; and repair, requalification, cost, and cross-laboratory transfer. It separates electromagnetic optical force from thermal convection, surface adhesion, Brownian motion, and sensor-induced artefacts. Strong comparators include calibrated free-space optical tweezers and spatial-light-modulator trapping configurations at matched specimen exposure and operational throughput. The book contains 30 mathematics-linked derivational routes, 82 chapters with 410 independently paginated research sections, 200 detailed future Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. A companion Excel atlas links each research chapter, quantitative candidate, test protocol, falsifier and external DOI evidence record. Publisher-identified publications on integrated optical phased arrays, silicon-photonic trapping, and photonics packaging inform the research boundary but are not treated as proof that the integrated microrobotic platform proposed here has already been demonstrated. The primary design principle is independent reproducibility: a controller should never be allowed to certify its own sensor output, ignore lost agents, or authorize a restart after a failed optical-power or thermal ledger. Negative studies, matched classical successes, and failed module integrations are retained as useful successor research evidence. This work offers testable possibilities for future investigation; it is not a claim of experimentally demonstrated autonomous nanorobots, and it has not undergone external peer review.

items.summary: Physical plausibility is essential for realistic video generation. Existing methods impose physical guidance before synthesis via simulations or refined prompts, but this can limit dynamic diversity, miss errors that emerge only after generation, and require repeated regeneration when inconsistencies remain. We therefore study a generate-diagnose-repair paradigm that preserves the original generation capability and selectively repairs physical inconsistencies afterward, raising two key questions: what to repair and how to repair? To address them, we introduce PhysRepair, an agentic video generation framework that combines causal reasoning over the observed physical failure with prior repair experience to enable localized and adaptive correction. Specifically, Spatiotemporal Causal Constraints identify the first invalid physical state and its causally affected states, producing a repair specification that guides physically plausible local regeneration while preserving unaffected content. Experience-augmented In-context Learning combines the ongoing repair context with relevant experience from previous repairs, allowing the agent to adapt its repair decisions across diverse physical failures and accumulate completed trajectories for future cases. Experiments on Physics-IQ Verified across solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics, thermodynamics, and magnetism demonstrate that PhysRepair consistently improves the physical plausibility of generated videos over existing methods. Our project page is available at https://xxkkxxx.github.io/PhysRepair-Website/.
items.title: Agentic Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reasoning

items.summary: Reviewed computational reproduction artifact for Fixed-Reference Scoring for Task-Consistent RUL Model Selection under Tunable Target Capping , version 2026.10.18-rc1. The archive contains author software, study configurations and selection records, 210 successful result records representing 320 fits, derived validation and standard-test predictions, thirteen reproducible manuscript summaries, and eight predefined checkpoint-audit cases. The eight distributed weights reproduced 1,414 archived inference outputs exactly in the recorded environment. Recomputing the reported summaries requires no raw NASA data. Fresh inference and training require separately obtained, hash-checked NASA C-MAPSS data; official links and checksums are included. Raw NASA files, preprocessed sensor features, installed dependencies, private logs and the other 632 weights are excluded. License scope: author software and software documentation are licensed under MIT. Author-derived predictions, configuration datasets and the eight selected weights are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). These licenses apply to their respective components, as specified in LICENSE and DATA_AND_WEIGHTS_LICENSE.md; NASA and other third-party rights remain separate. The standard test data had been inspected during earlier development. These outcomes are conditional descriptive evidence. Fixed-reference scoring is not consistently better than fixed cap125, model-seed tests do not establish conventional significance, and the 30-cycle maintenance-delay proxy does not improve. The original-precision FD002 cap125 failure and separate FP32-attention sensitivity are retained distinctly. Historical paths and preparation-status files are preserved as build provenance, not claims about current publication status. AI assistance is documented in the included assistance record. Code repository: https://github.com/KKevinZhou/fixed-reference-rul-model-selection
items.title: Fixed-Reference Scoring for Task-Consistent RUL Model Selection under Tunable Target Capping — Code and Derived Predictions

items.summary: Speculative decoding typically characterizes speedup by draft tokens accepted per verification round. Lossless verification preserves the target model's output distribution and thus expected completion length, making this metric a meaningful efficiency proxy. Relaxed (lossy) verification accepts tokens that lossless verification would reject, potentially altering that distribution. We identify a length inflation phenomenon: relaxed verification lengthens completions, primarily by extending reasoning traces, largely offsetting apparent gains in accepted tokens per round. We evaluate existing training-free relaxed verification rules on twelve target-drafter pairs against lossless verification on identical prompts, measuring completion length, verifier rounds, wall-clock time, and task accuracy. At each rule's most relaxed evaluated setting, relaxed verification on average accepts $1.34\times$ as many tokens per round but produces $1.54\times$ longer completions. For rules with higher acceptance lengths, tokens accepted only under relaxed verification tend to have low target-model probability, contributing to length inflation. For rules that reduce verifier rounds, accuracy typically drops substantially. Further analysis traces some failures to continued reasoning that exhausts the budget needed to deliver a final answer. Overall, accepted tokens per round alone is an unreliable measure of decoding speed under relaxed verification. Completion length and verifier rounds must also be reported to assess actual efficiency.
items.title: Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding

items.summary: Notes cover the changes since 0.5.0. pip install metabeta==0.6.0 Tutorials Three notebooks in demos/ replace intro.ipynb and priors.ipynb . Each runs on a CPU runtime in Colab. 01-quickstart : lme4's sleepstudy end to end, next to lme4's estimates. 02-families : Bernoulli ( cbpp ) and Poisson ( Salamanders ) fits, posterior predictive checks, and random-walk moves next to a NUTS reference. 03-priors : prior specification, prior sensitivity in one call, and model comparison by Bayes factors. New reports posteriorDraws(result) : posterior draws of the global parameters on the data's scale, as a DataFrame named as in posteriorSummary (#31). groupDraws(result) : each group's coefficients per draw, the fixed effect plus the group's deviation (#33). posteriorPredictive(result) : the observed responses and one replicate per posterior draw, in the data's units (#33). bayesFactor(result, reference) : the Bayes factor of one model over another, per prior, with its Kass–Raftery grade; both results come from sample(evidence=True) (#33). sample n_samples defaults to 1,000 draws (#19). seed= makes a call reproducible and leaves the caller's random stream untouched (#32). posteriorPredictive and plotPPD take seed= too (#26, #33). Every summary ends with a fit metric: R² (Gaussian), AUC (Bernoulli) or deviance (Poisson) (#29). loo=True adds PSIS-LOO to the summary; it replaces diagnostics=True (#29). random_walk=True runs silently and warns only below an IMH effective sample size (ESS) of 10 (#29). Warnings state the failure, its consequence and numbered remedies, and point at the user's call (#18, #29). The first call after loading costs about as much as a warm one; warmup() runs that pass explicitly (#19). Formulas, scales and names Formulas follow lme4: y ~ 1 + (1 | g) fits an intercept-only model, preprocessing reads only the columns the formula names, and column names keep their case (#15). The order of fixed terms no longer changes the fit; names are mapped back in every output (#16). Summaries default to x_scale='original' . Random-effect SDs, correlations and per-group effects are on the data's scale like the fixed effects, and so are the prior lines (#17). rfxSummary labels each group correctly (#17). Api.from_pretrained('gaussian') is an alias of 'normal' , in any case (#30). Reports pick a dataset row by prior_id , a prior's name or its index (#32). Errors Unsupported formula syntax raises NotImplementedError with a workaround: || , nested or crossed grouping factors, interactions ( : , * ) and function calls such as log() or factor() (#18). Data outside every submodel's range raises one ValueError that names the limits; a family mismatch names the checkpoint to load (#18). A named predictor dropped as collinear or near-constant raises an error that names it (#18). Formulas the pretrained models cannot fit raise an error that names the fix: a random intercept without a fixed one, or the reverse, and a random slope that is not a fixed term (#16). GPU from_pretrained(..., device='cuda') works on GPUs whose torch build lacks a cholesky_solve kernel, such as Colab's T4 with torch 2.11 for CUDA 13 (#26). plotParameters and sample(loo=True) work on a CUDA device (#26). Packaging Python 3.13 support, with dependency floors at Colab's preinstalled versions (#20). The code is licensed under Apache-2.0, previously CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (#21). CITATION.cff drives GitHub's citation button (#21). Deprecated, removed in 0.7 Each alias still works and raises a FutureWarning (#29, #32). sample(diagnostics=True) : use loo=True . batch_index= in posteriorSummary and rfxSummary , and index= in plotParameters : use prior_id= . indices= in plotPPD : use prior_ids= .
items.title: metabeta: amortized Bayesian inference for generalized linear mixed-effects models

items.summary: We develop a counterfactual semantics based on reopening partial information states. Evaluation first removes enough stated content to leave the antecedent’s attributes unresolved, retaining what the chosen scope protects, then asserts the antecedent and considers the surviving consistent refinements. Would and might quantify over the admissible alternatives; a weighted extension supplies graded evaluations. The principal result concerns finite models with fully supported residues. When a conjunctive antecedent reopens each constituent attribute, adding a supported conjunct can remove the grounds of another conclusion. A four-attribute countermodel therefore violates Cautious Monotony, excluding any smooth preferential representation that preserves the evaluable verdicts. We also establish a sufficient nesting condition for Cut and exhibit its failure without that condition. The conjunctive reopening rule is an explicit interpretive commitment; its suitability for ordinary-language counterfactuals remains an empirical question. The account uses declared dependencies, scope restrictions, and priorities, while the quantitative extension assumes a weight kernel. Comparisons with belief revision, premise semantics, update semantics, and causal intervention identify the consequences of reopening an attribute rather than merely making its proposed value consistent with retained information.
items.title: Counterfactual Evaluation by Reopening Information States

items.summary: Laser cladding enables bi-material components with tailored surface properties, but cyclic loading makes fatigue resistance of the whole component critical. This study examined the bending fatigue life (R = 0.1) of unalloyed steels S235J2 and S355J2 and high-strength steels S460NL and S690QL clad with aluminium bronze Metco 51NS, a combination typical of tube-bending mandrels. Results were evaluated as force amplitude versus cycles to failure using a Basquin-type power law. Fatigue strength at 10⁷ cycles was 4.0, 3.4, 3.8 and 4.5 kN, respectively, so high-strength steels performed only slightly better or similarly. Cracks always initiated on the surface of the cladding and crossed the defect-free interface. The base material is therefore not decisive for fatigue life, which is governed by the surface layer, provided cladding parameters are optimal. Less expensive unalloyed steels are thus sufficient for such components.
items.title: Fatigue resistance of structural steels coated with aluminium bronze using laser cladding

items.summary: LLM agents increasingly use retrieval tools across languages, yet their safety evaluation remains English-centric. It remains unclear whether language affects tool admission, post-retrieval generation, or both. We independently vary request, retrieved-page, and required response languages in a controlled URL-retrieval setting across ten models and seven languages. We identify Safety Loss through Interlingual Processing (SLIP). Non-English harmful requests increase mean tool admission from 46.9% to 67.4%, with a positive mean change in every model. This pattern also persists in an autonomous retrieval setup across all four models tested in this setting. Requiring answers in the page language increases pooled harmfulness on matched tool calls from 50.3% to 57.4% across four closed-weight models, mainly in Chinese and Hindi. Translating pages alone produces no consistent harm increase in eight models with comparable inference settings. Automated audits show that a non-harmful response may be a genuine safety refusal, a deflection citing language difficulties, or an unusable answer. Harmfulness labels alone cannot distinguish these outcomes. Multilingual safety evaluations should therefore measure tool admission and response harmfulness separately and distinguish refusal from capability failure.
items.title: Disentangling Language Effects on Tool Admission and Post-Retrieval Safety

items.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have significantly advanced instruction-driven perception through the "Embedding-as-Mask" paradigm. However, extending this capability to Remote Sensing (RS) reasoning segmentation remains exceptionally challenging under cluttered geographical contexts and extreme scale variations, often leading to Spatial Fidelity Degradation and Target Misidentification. We identify a critical yet underexplored bottleneck: the sequential alienation of the segmentation token [SEG] from its initial visual grounding within the autoregressive generation paradigm. Produced only at the end of long reasoning chains, [SEG] relies on visual evidence that has been progressively diluted by linguistic abstraction and autoregressive noise. This information decay is particularly catastrophic for RS targets with minuscule pixel footprints, where even marginal fidelity loss leads to localization failure. To address these bottlenecks, we propose GeoReason, a novel framework designed to fortify logical deduction and preserve spatial integrity. First, we introduce an Anticipatory Prior mechanism that injects the [SEG] token directly into the initial user query, shifting it from a terminal output to a primary condition. This paradigm shift transforms the token into a persistent spatial anchor, preventing information decay during long-form linguistic inference. Second, we enhance visual reasoning via a Location-aware Chain-of-Thought (CoT) that enforces coarse-to-fine localization using bounding boxes, coupled with a Latent Patch-to-Token Alignment (PTA) Loss that explicitly aligns the latent segmentation token with physical RS textures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GeoReason consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the Earthreason and RRSIS-D benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/Fanc0126/GeoReason.
items.title: GeoReason: Bridging Logical Reasoning and Spatial Fidelity in Remote Sensing Segmentation

items.summary: This dataset is a consolidated, machine-readable record of tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) in Poland from 1998 to 2024, assembled from official publicly-available surveillance products and used as the analytic base for an accompanying surveillance article in preparation for Eurosurveillance. For each of Poland's 16 voivodeships (NUTS-2 administrative regions) and for the country as a whole, the dataset contains: annual notified TBE case counts; quarterly breakdown of cases by onset (Q1–Q4); annual incidence per 100,000 inhabitants; hospitalised case counts and percentages; and annual TBE vaccination registrations, stratified by age (0–19, 20+, total). Case data are drawn from the National Institute of Public Health–National Institute of Hygiene (NIZP-PZH) biweekly bulletin Meldunki epidemiologiczne; vaccination data from the NIZP-PZH annual report Szczepienia ochronne w Polsce; population denominators from the Central Statistical Office of Poland (GUS). Vaccination figures count persons completing the primary three-dose cycle or receiving a booster, not total doses. Released under CC BY 4.0. See README for full column dictionary, scope, and known limitations. An accompanying Python script reproduces the four manuscript figures directly from this dataset. Version 2.0 accompanies the revised manuscript (October 2026): adds the ECDC Atlas extract, administrative boundary file, revision analyses (including negative binomial models with estimated dispersion) and scripts generating Figures 1–5. See CHANGES_v2.0.md.
items.title: Tick-borne encephalitis in Poland, 1998–2024: master surveillance dataset

items.summary: This report consolidates six numerical and derived consistency checks examining amplitude–phase representations of string-theory scattering within the Harmonic Physics research programme. The calculations cover two-magnon Bethe–Yang quantization in the AFS approximation (BY01), three-particle Yang–Baxter consistency for a supplied string-frame su(2|2) matrix (YB01), fundamental BES dressing-factor crossing (CP01), scalar bound-state fusion (BF01), bound-state crossing (BC01), and derived double-crossing consistency (DC01). The report presents 31 referenced equations, declared sample sets, numerical results, convergence checks and deliberately altered controls. Particular attention is given to preserving calculated amplitudes alongside phases, distinguishing coherent channel sums from scalar products, and retaining matrix-frame conventions and analytic continuation information. All six entries satisfy their declared numerical acceptance criteria. The fundamental and bound-state crossing calculations construct the continued factors independently of their target crossing equations. Double crossing is explicitly classified as a derived consistency check because its second continuation is imposed through the crossing functional equation. The accompanying reproducibility package includes the original calculation scripts, protocols, result tables, equation sources, checksums and a combined runner. A fresh integrated run successfully reproduced all five checkpoint programs covering the six entries. These results establish bounded mathematical correspondences with supplied string-theory models over the tested domains. They do not independently derive Phase dynamics, predict formation probabilities, or validate an internal nesting wavefunction. The report provides a compact equation register for carrying the supported correspondences into the broader Phase framework while preserving their provenance and limitations.
items.title: String Scattering in Amplitude and Phase

items.summary: Optimizing product listings for generative search requires language agents not only to rewrite effectively but also to continually self-improve by retaining successful strategies across diverse categories. However, existing approaches often treat structured listings as free-form text, leaving effective strategies implicit in prompts, search trajectories, or rewritten outputs rather than accumulating them as a reusable agentic memory. To address this limitation, we introduce GLOBE, an agentic framework that drives continual self-improvement by storing optimization knowledge in an evolving handbook of explicit, field-scoped behaviors. In each episode, an Editor applies relevant behaviors and receives rank-based feedback, which a Reflector converts into behavior updates. Crucially for dependable execution in real-world settings, a Moderator removes redundant proposals, a Curator commits accepted changes, and consistently harmful behaviors are deactivated. This cycle transforms episodic feedback into a persistent, field-scoped optimization memory. Experiments show that structured behaviors outperform monolithic prompt optimization, while feedback-driven evolution and moderation further improve effectiveness and reduce downside risk. The learned behaviors also remain effective on unseen product categories, suggesting that agentic memory evolution supports interpretable and transferable product optimization.
items.title: GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search

items.summary: This record accompanies the two-dimensional supplement to A gauge-invariant measure for lattice chiral fermions by Nathaniel Craig. It contains the supplement and its LaTeX source, together with the curated core reproducibility package, supplied in 65 standard tar.gz core archives and a separate evidence addendum. The supplement studies a two-dimensional chiral SU(5) theory with three conjugate-5 left-handed fermions, one 10 right-handed fermion, and five right-handed singlets. It presents an analytic measure construction on a specified admissible domain and numerical tests of selected currents, gauge responses, and determinant phases. The core archive contains all 74 scientific evidence references cited in the supplement, scientific implementations, the complete free-gap ledger, and the saved inputs needed for three principal scalar replays. It retains reports on other calculations and their limitations, but does not contain every raw matrix or intermediate record for those calculations. Extract all 65 archives into one directory to recover the complete core and run the documented checks. The remainder of the additional-data collection and the superseded full calculation archive are not included. The supported replays check saved evidence and recompute final scalar arithmetic; they do not rerun every historical current integration or matrix calculation. A separate gap replay checks the covering and residual bounds using implementation code shared with the producer. The README, result index, completeness record, manifests, and verification receipts specify the procedures and limits. These two-dimensional checks support, but do not prove, the four-dimensional result. The evidence addendum supplies 123 further scientific files referenced by the reports, including exact error ledgers, control results, fields, plots, and compact input records. Extract it alongside the 65 core archives and follow the updated README. Its verifier checks the added-file hashes and selected exact saved arithmetic for the finite-amplitude two-step curl and direct B1 endpoint comparison. It does not rerun the original matrix calculations or establish the analytic remainder estimate. License scope: Apache-2.0 for project-authored code; CC BY 4.0 for project-generated data and written documentation. Existing third-party licenses and notices remain in force. See LICENSES.txt.
items.title: Two-dimensional chiral SU(5) measure and calculation records for A gauge-invariant measure for lattice chiral fermions

items.summary: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. It pairs multiple-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free-form visual question answering (VQA) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality. Across 12 proprietary, open-weight, and driving-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT-6-Astra, achieves only 43.4% average multiple-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random-choice baseline. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal.
items.title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases

items.summary: Learning causal structure from data requires assumptions about mechanisms, noises, observation schemes, and interventions. Historically, causal discovery has relied primarily on conditional independence. This review focuses on modern causal discovery methods that exploit properties of distributions beyond conditional independence. Our organizing principle separates the source of identification from the statistical estimator and its computational implementation. This perspective connects conditional-independence methods with distributional asymmetries, conditional-moment restrictions, and variation across environments or individuals. We examine discovery under latent confounding and feedback, distinguishing causal information about observed variables from reconstruction of latent structure and emphasizing the additional semantics required by cyclic models. We also distinguish population identification, frequentist and Bayesian consistency, uncertainty quantification, and algorithmic guarantees. Throughout, examples show why the same observational distribution can support different conclusions under different model classes. We conclude with guidance for comparing methods at their identifiable targets and a research agenda for uncertainty, heterogeneous populations, non-scalar variables, and the intersection of discrete data, feedback, and hidden confounding.
items.title: Causal Discovery beyond Conditional Independence: Identifiability, Algorithms, and Statistical Inference for Directed Acyclic and Cyclic Graphs

items.summary: This record holds the preregistration, code, outputs, process logs and session transcripts of a study that is also a meta-experiment on research produced almost entirely by an AI agent (Claude, model claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic, run in Claude Code) under the direction of one researcher. The substantive study asks a deliberately implausible question: is living with a cat associated with untreated dental decay among US adults? It uses public data from NHANES 2005–2006 with survey-weighted modified Poisson regression, prespecified confounders, sensitivity analyses and equivalence testing. The preregistered primary result was inconclusive (prevalence ratio 1.12, 95% CI 0.93 to 1.36). The meta-experiment measures what producing the study took: time, human interventions, agent errors and the share of code and text written by the agent. The accompanying preprint, "Do cats rot your teeth? A by-the-book paper written by an AI agent, and what it means for scientific communication", shows how four of the 45 preregistered estimates could support a positive paper without breaking the registration, and argues that verification, not writing, is now the bottleneck of scientific communication. Version 1 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23435708) is the frozen preregistration, deposited before any exposure–outcome association was computed and later registered on OSF (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/RVH7J). Its files remain available in version 1. items.title: Do cats rot your teeth? Preregistration, code, outputs, process logs and transcripts of a study produced by an AI agent (NHANES 2005–2006)

items.summary: Cross-Lingual Jailbreak Evaluation — Final Thesis Data and Outputs This archive accompanies the master's thesis Multilingual Jailbreaks in Language-Specific Large Language Models (Gabriel de Jesus Coelho da Silva; advisor Carlos Becker Westphall; Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina, 2026). It contains the study's frozen source-run files and the final thesis analysis release. The source-run files remain unchanged. The study evaluates eight instruction-tuned assistants in four language-matched pairs aligned with Portuguese, Italian, Swedish, and Bulgarian, plus a separate English reference model. StrongREJECT harmful prompts were translated into thirteen attack languages with NLLB-200, submitted to the models, and scored using the official StrongREJECT evaluator after response back-translation where applicable. The analysis combines URIEL+ featural angular distance, BELEBELE-derived IF/CONS/SPEC, and tokenizer diagnostics. The final behavioral results report the graded StrongREJECT score. The choice of this graded outcome and its fractional-logit GEE analysis followed inspection of results and was not pre-specified. Historical binary outputs remain available as provenance, not as the reported thesis results. Files added in this version File Contents final_analysis_dataset.parquet Final prompt/model/language analysis dataset, including scored responses, graded outcomes, joined predictors, coverage, and exclusion fields. final_analysis_dataset.jsonl.gz Compressed JSONL form of the same analysis release. belebele_canonical_mapping.csv Mapping of saved BELEBELE prediction rows to canonical question identities. belebele_specialization.jsonl Per-model/language IF, CONS, and SPEC from the saved generation-parsed predictions. final_analysis_supporting.zip Quality and coverage records, graded result tables and diagnostics, inference robustness analyses, translation and scoring provenance, and reported BELEBELE examples. Paths mirror the evaluation repository. README_FINAL_DATA.md , PROVENANCE.json , SHA256SUMS.txt Reading guide, source-file and archive-member provenance, and SHA-256 checksums. For the reported graded results, use the release folders under outputs/releases/2026-09-29-graded-reporting/ and outputs/releases/2026-10-16-inference-robustness/ in final_analysis_supporting.zip . The companion evaluation code is at https://github.com/gabrieljcs/ufsc-thesis (commit 4a9a84a36342f022bf99eeb1dc4e7606028bf7d4 ). PROVENANCE.json identifies the local source and SHA-256 digest for each new upload and each file inside the supporting archive. Measurement and validation limits. BELEBELE option-likelihood rescoring is specified in code but was not run for this thesis; the supplied IF/CONS/SPEC values use the generation-parsed instrument. The completed prompt QC used a BLASER gate and an uncalibrated LLM scalar audit of flagged translations. Human bilingual prompt and response audits, trusted-reference spBLEU, and MultiJail validation
items.title: Cross-Lingual Jailbreak Evaluation

items.summary: Code and data accompanying Pan, L., "Where does detrital-zircon source unmixing break? An analytic identifiability criterion and its large-scale Monte-Carlo verification for NMF provenance unmixing" (submitted to Sedimentary Geology). Reproduces every figure: the synthetic data generator, the HPC scan harness (supervised and unsupervised KL-NMF), the merge and figure-generation scripts, the identifiability-theory verification scripts (direct sigma_err measurement on the (rho, n) plane) and their bias/RMSE decomposition, the per-axis results, the per-cell 3D phase-atlas summary, and the real-sample a-priori screen (Fig. 8) with fifteen real per-grain detrital-zircon age samples (Cretaceous Songliao Basin; Jurassic-Lower Cretaceous northern North China Craton margin). Code and synthetic results: MIT licence. The real age samples are redistributed under their original CC BY 4.0 licences (OneDZ, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15522949; Puetz et al., Figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.24852987.v1) with per-sample attribution; they are not re-licensed as MIT. v1.2.1 adds selected supplementary numerical probes, small historical summaries, atlas generator/HPC wrapper/merge, explicit Fig.3 command and seed verification, BU21 bibliography, and the submitted-a Fig.1 label, source-verified real-sample record corrections (05FW007; 100821-1/-3) with a re-rendered Fig. 8, conditional in-figure wording for Figs 3 and 8, and verified dataset licences. Historical probe comments describe exploratory models; theory_checks/README.md states their current scope and verification limits. The full per-seed atlas raw (559 MB; 187 MB gzipped) is not included. No separate public archive DOI was found in the project records searched; these raw data are not publicly archived in a verified record and may be requested from the author.
items.title: Applicability boundaries of NMF detrital-zircon unmixing — reproducibility package

items.summary: This dataset contains numerical simulation results underlying Figures 3–11, Supplementary Figures S1–S6, and Supplementary Tables S1–S4 of the associated manuscript. The simulations examine sampling-induced concentration bias in suction-lysimeter measurements of PFOS, PFOA, and PFPeA in sandy loam and sandy clay. The archive includes baseline hydrologic and concentration series, equilibrium sampling results, displayed spatial fields, adsorption-kinetics scenarios, vacuum-operation comparisons, single- and dual-chamber water and concentration histories, cumulative PFOS mass-discharge estimates, supplementary flow diagnostics, and reported model parameters and sampling dates. The package contains eight Excel workbooks, one spatial CSV file, two daily atmospheric input CSV files with a text guide, a README, calculation notes, and file checksums. The input files are exact copies of the processed daily forcing used by the model for the long-term loading and one-year baseline/sampling simulations; their column definitions, units, uses and source attribution are documented in the meteorological-input folder. File-to-figure mappings, units, and calculation conventions are described in the included documentation. Figures 1 and 2 are conceptual and mesh illustrations and have no independent numerical result tables in this archive. Executable simulation and plotting code and full internal model output histories are not included. The archived numerical values support reconstruction of the reported data displays and recalculation of the reported comparisons; they are not a complete model-rerun package.
items.title: Numerical data for: Quantifying sampling-induced concentration bias in suction-lysimeter measurements of PFAS porewater concentration in the vadose zone

items.summary: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) are flexible priors for compositional regression functions, but inference for intermediate layers faces questions. The basic obstruction is an adjacent-layer symmetry: applying an invertible transformation and its inverse to two adjacent layers leaves the composed regression map unchanged. Under explicit symmetry and prior-comparability conditions, we show that the posterior may not concentrate on any prescribed intermediate-layer representation, even when the composed regression function is estimable. We then introduce an augmented $ρ$-fractional posterior that reweights layer decompositions by a non-saturating identity-deviation penalty. The augmentation changes posterior odds between symmetry-related decompositions by an exponential penalty ratio. Under proper choices of the penalty and a prior mass condition, it preserves function-level fractional posterior contraction, while shrinking the redundant layers towards the identity mapping. Thus, the likelihood does not identify a unique ``true'' set of layers; the augmentation favors identity-biased parsimonious decompositions within an equivalence class of layers; uniqueness of a selected representative is not established.
items.title: Canonical Layer Inference for Deep Gaussian Processes via Symmetry-Breaking Augmentation

items.summary: Resampling is the standard remedy for weight degeneracy in particle filters, but in high dimensions it distorts the spectrum of the ensemble covariance in a way that is computable from the importance weights. This paper studies the inverse problem: recovering the pre-resampling spectrum from the observed weights and the empirical spectrum alone, and using it without biasing the filter. We first show that the forward spectral law extends to random importance weights once one conditions on the weights together with the realized offspring counts, rather than on the weights alone. We then construct a regularized free-deconvolution estimator, prove its consistency with an explicit error budget at a fixed resolution scale, and certify model mismatch through a computable forward residual. The repaired spectrum enters the filter only as the preconditioner of a Metropolis-adjusted rejuvenation move, so that spectral error affects mixing efficiency but not the invariant target. For the full filtering cycle, we derive a geometrically summable error recursion under stable scalar dynamics and an explicit law for the cost of abstaining from repair. Pre-registered simulations show that the inversion reduces the spectral error by an order of magnitude, that the corrected preconditioner recovers about 90% of the oracle's sampling efficiency in an anisotropic regime, and that the cost of abstention depends on when abstentions occur rather than on how many. The repair recovers eigenvalue laws, not eigenvectors, and is certified only within an explicitly stated exogenous-weight regime.
items.title: Regularized free deconvolution for spectral repair of resampling distortion in high-dimensional particle filters

items.summary: Lecture 1 formulated the recommendation problem in abstract terms: a set of users U , a set of items I , and a preference function r(u,i) that must be estimated for the pairs that have not been observed. Every algorithm studied in this course, however, operates on concrete data rather than on abstractions. The quality of a recommender system is therefore bounded by the quality, the structure, and the representation of the data from which it learns. In practice, improving the data frequently brings larger gains than changing the algorithm. A sophisticated model trained on noisy, biased, or poorly prepared data produces poor recommendations, a principle often summarized as garbage in, garbage out . This lecture therefore addresses three questions: è Which data does a recommender system collect, and what do these data really mean? è How can these data be organized and represented so that algorithms can process them? è How must the data be prepared and partitioned before a model is built and assessed? After studying this lecture, the reader should be able to: · Identify the sources and categories of data used in a recommender system; · Characterize explicit and implicit feedback, including their strengths and weaknesses; · Construct a user–item matrix and interpret its sparsity; · Represent users and items as vectors built from interactions and descriptive features; · Apply the main preprocessing operations to ratings and implicit signals; · Split a dataset correctly and avoid information leakage. The path followed by the data throughout this lecture is: Data sources → Feedback signals → User–item matrix → Vector representations → Preprocessing → Data splitting
items.title: Lecture Notes on Recommender Systems

items.summary: Student-built load banks used in undergraduate electrical machines laboratories typically derive rotor speed from a slotted-disc tachometer whose pulse train is quantised by a fixed sampling clock, and the resulting slip estimate feeds directly into the torque-speed curve that students report. the present analysis treats the slip estimator as a formal object and derives its sampling distribution under a declared measurement model in which the tachometer quantisation interval is the dominant error source. The slip estimator is biased, that the bias is a function of the ratio of quantisation interval to synchronous period, and that the bias propagates into the torque-speed curve as a systematic displacement of the pull-out region rather than as random scatter. A replication-based evaluation was conducted: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2), and the ordinary least squares estimator was characterised under the stated process. The estimated bias for the intercept was -0.02315 and for the exposure coefficient 0.00064; the root mean squared errors were 0.88484 and 0.01581 respectively; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that the estimator is essentially unbiased for the slope but that the intercept carries a small negative displacement, and that the quantisation mechanism identified analytically is consistent with the direction and magnitude of the observed intercept bias. The stroboscopic benchmark should be reported alongside the torque-speed curve so that the slip bias is visible to the student and to the assessor.
tags: induction motor; slip estimation; tachometer quantisation; torque-speed curve; engineering education
items.title: Induction-Motor Slip Estimation Bias in Student-Built Engineering Education Load Banks: A Stroboscopic Speed Benchmark Linking Tachometer Quantization to Torque-Speed Curve Reliability
